name: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
principle: The code uses values that are predictable or low-entropy where security depends on unpredictability. Attackers can guess tokens, keys, IVs, nonces, or identifiers and bypass protection mechanisms.
detection_signals: C/C++ rand(), random(), drand48(), lrand48(), or std::rand() used to build session, token, csrf, reset, key, iv, nonce, salt, or password values
Java java.util.Random, java.lang.Math.random(), or ThreadLocalRandom used to build session, token, csrf, reset, key, iv, nonce, salt, or password values
srand(time(NULL)), srand(getpid()), srand(userId), Random.setSeed(System.currentTimeMillis()), or fixed numeric seed before security value generation
random output reduced to a small range with % N, nextInt(N), or substring truncation for security codes or tokens
custom PRNG such as LCG/XorShift/Mersenne Twister used for authentication, authorization, key generation, IV, nonce, or reset code
security-sensitive random value generated without SecureRandom, getrandom(), /dev/urandom, arc4random_buf(), BCryptGenRandom(), CryptGenRandom(), or RAND_bytes
negative_signals: Java SecureRandom used for token, key, IV, nonce, salt, or reset code generation
C/C++ getrandom(), arc4random_buf(), BCryptGenRandom(), CryptGenRandom(), or RAND_bytes used and return status is checked
random value is only for simulation, testing, UI effects, load balancing, or games and is not used as a security secret
seed is obtained from an OS CSPRNG and not from time, PID, username, user ID, or constants
security token has sufficient byte length, e.g. 128 bits or more from a CSPRNG before encoding
false_defense_traps: Using rand(), java.util.Random, or Math.random because results look statistically random
Seeding with current time, PID, username, user ID, MAC address, or a constant
Hashing or Base64-encoding weak PRNG output and treating it as unpredictable
Generating a CSPRNG value and then truncating it to a short numeric code without rate limiting
Using UUIDs or sequential IDs as secrets without verifying they are CSPRNG-backed and sufficiently long
verification_focus: Does any security-sensitive value that must be unguessable come from a non-CSPRNG, predictable seed, small value space, or invariant algorithm?

consequence_chains.trigger: security token or key generated with statistical PRNG API
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker predicts values and bypasses authentication or authorization

consequence_chains.trigger: PRNG seeded with time, PID, user ID, constant, or reused seed
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker reproduces the PRNG sequence and guesses secrets

consequence_chains.trigger: security code or token drawn from a small range
CAPTCHA challenge generated from guessable random values

patch_principle: Use a CSPRNG for all security-sensitive random values.
Use well-vetted implementations such as Java SecureRandom, getrandom(), arc4random_buf(), BCryptGenRandom(), CryptGenRandom(), or RAND_bytes.
Seed only from high-quality entropy sources; do not use time, PID, user ID, constants, or reusable seeds.
Use sufficient output length, commonly at least 128 bits for tokens and appropriate sizes for keys, IVs, nonces, and salts.
Check CSPRNG API return values and fail closed if randomness cannot be obtained.
